1 · Matching

Each molecule finds its spectrum

molecule A → spectrum_3
molecule B → spectrum_2
molecule C → spectrum_1

Method: Trotter circuits (300 steps of 2.5 ms), all 2N X-basis initial states, Qiskit Estimator, Fourier transform. Similarity is the cosine similarity of the two spectra on a common ppm grid: 0.78 to 0.83 for the three matches, below 0.01 for every other pair.

2 · Noise sweep

Peaks survive until the line width reaches the smallest line spacing

MoleculeJ couplings [Hz]Smallest spacing we resolve, ΔνminMaximum noise_strength, ΓmaxLine width there, Γmax/π
A0.9, 11.8, 17.96.1 Hz20.5 s−16.5 Hz
B0.5, 8.6, 15.67.0 Hz23.5 s−17.5 Hz
C7.97.9 Hz24.5 s−17.8 Hz
Γmax ≈ π × Δνmin
  1. noise_strength Γ multiplies the signal by e−Γt.
  2. After the Fourier transform every line is a Lorentzian of full width Γ/π (in Hz).
  3. Two lines Δν apart merge when that width reaches Δν, so Γ/π ≈ Δν.

Sweep from 0.1 to 100 s−1. A peak counts as resolved if it rises at least 5% of the tallest peak above the valley next to it. With 0.75 s of signal the useful range is about 5 to 20–25 s−1: below 5 the signal is cut off before it has decayed, above the maximum the lines merge.

3 · Discussion: missing peaks

Molecule A has 15 lines. The reference shows 12, we show 8.

15

transitions are allowed by theory (exact diagonalisation).

→
12

in the reference: three are combination lines 104 to 105 times weaker.

→
8

in our spectrum: four pairs lie 0.9 Hz apart, and 0.75 s of signal resolves only 1.33 Hz.

→
12

again when we simulate 4 s of signal instead of 0.75 s.

It is the signal length, not Trotter error

  • Frequency resolution is 1 / signal length: 0.75 s gives 1.33 Hz.
  • Exact evolution with the same 0.75 s also shows only 8 peaks.
  • The price of 4 s: 1600 Trotter steps instead of 300, so much deeper circuits.

Why are the three noise maxima so similar? Each is π times the smallest spacing we can resolve: 6.1, 7.0 and 7.9 Hz. These are ordinary proton couplings or the difference of two (17.9 − 11.8, 15.6 − 8.6, 7.9). The couplings that would set the molecules apart (0.9 Hz in A, 0.5 Hz in B) are below our resolution.

4 · Discussion: Trotter error

Trotter error moves the lines, it does not blur them

  • A Trotter step replaces e−iHΔt by a product of simple rotations. Because the terms of H do not commute, the product is the exact evolution of a slightly different Hamiltonian.
  • A different Hamiltonian has different energy levels, so every line is displaced: up to 0.72 Hz at our 2.5 ms step.
  • Each hydrogen's group of lines moves as a block (+0.7, −0.1, −0.6 Hz). Spacings inside a group change by at most 0.12 Hz, so the J pattern, the matching and the noise limits are unaffected.
Time stepLargest line shiftSteps for 0.75 s
2.5 ms0.72 Hz300
1.25 ms0.14 Hz600
0.625 ms0.03 Hz1200

Halving the step cuts the shift 4 to 5 times (roughly step2) but doubles the circuit depth.

5 · Real hardware: what we ran

Taking molecule C from the simulator to a real device

1 · SAME CIRCUITSThe notebook's Trotter step for molecule C: 2 spins, so 2 qubits.
2 · ONE INITIAL STATEOnly |++⟩. |−−⟩ gives the same contribution; |+−⟩ and |−+⟩ have zero weight.
3 · BEST QUBIT PAIRLowest two-qubit gate error among pairs with readout error below 1%.
4 · NATIVE GATESTranslated to the device's gates and checked noise-free: agreement to 10−13.
5 · RUN300 time points, 500 shots each, no error mitigation. Then the same Fourier transform.

Version 1: short circuits

All Trotter steps up to time point k are multiplied into one 4×4 matrix, and any two-qubit operation needs at most 3 two-qubit gates. The matrix is worked out classically, so this does not scale.

Version 2: full Trotter depth

The Trotter step really runs k times, as it would for any larger molecule: 3, 450 and 897 two-qubit gates at time points 1, 150 and 299.

6 · Real hardware: results

Molecule C on a real quantum computer

Works: short circuits

  • Four peaks at 6.293, 6.309, 6.368, 6.384 ppm, the positions of the reference lines.
  • 93% of the signal amplitude kept; spectrum correlates 0.91 with the noise-free one.

Fails: full Trotter depth

  • Signal falls to 26% of its amplitude; peaks land at 6.31, 6.34, 6.44 ppm.
  • Gate errors move lines as well as damping them, which a decay like noise_strength cannot describe.

ibm_marrakesh (156 qubits, Heron r2), qubits 147 and 148, two-qubit gate error 0.12%. 300 time points, 500 shots, no error mitigation, 185 s of device time. Only the initial state |++⟩ is needed. Caveat: the short circuits exist because any two-qubit evolution compiles to 3 two-qubit gates, so the compiler has done the 4×4 evolution classically. This shows the pipeline on a device, not a scalable simulation.
